goals.use: A public npm library. The author's own app uses it as a normal dependency.
goals.scale: 500 columns x 100,000 rows. Initial render under 500ms, scrolling at about 60 frames per second on a normal laptop, search and filter results under 200ms.
goals.versioning: 0.x versions until all core epics are done. Breaking changes are allowed in 0.x. Then 1.0 with semantic versioning.

priorities.later: Wanted, low priority. Can come after 1.0.
priorities.future: Optional. Only if a real need appears.

decisions: Data lives in the browser first. The consumer passes all rows. Inside the table, data goes through fixed steps: search, filter, sort, paginate. A server mode can take over the same steps later.
The library ships its own UI (menus, popups, panels) with CSS the consumer can override. It is not headless.

Every user-changeable state (hidden columns, filters, sort, search text, page, collapsed groups) works in two modes: uncontrolled with a default value, and controlled with a value prop and a change callback.
Each column has a type: text, number, date or category. Filters, sorting and CSV export use the type.
Search and filters use the text the user sees, after custom render or format.
Pagination is an optional mode. The default is one scrolling list with virtual rendering.
passesRule: An epic has passes: true only when every acceptance item has an automated test that passes. The test name starts with the epic id, for example "E08: sorts 100,000 rows in under 200ms". Layout items use browser tests, speed items use the benchmark script. If a test of an epic fails, its passes value goes back to false.

epics.title: Base layout
epics.why: A table with fixed column widths that scrolls in both directions.
scope: Typed column config with fixed widths and a default width
Scroll container with optional maxVisibleHeight
Sticky header
Space for overlay scroll bars (macOS)
Message when there are no columns
acceptance: Each column uses its own width or the default width, and the table width is the sum of the column widths
With maxVisibleHeight, rows scroll inside the container
The header stays visible while rows scroll
Overlay scroll bars do not cover the last column or the last row when scrolled to the end
A table with no columns shows a "No columns" message

package.json fields: exports, types, peerDependencies on react and react-dom, files
Keep the demo app as a separate build that uses only the public API
Release steps for 0.x versions, with a changelog

react and react-dom are not part of the bundle

epics.title: Rendering spike: <table> or <div> grid
epics.why: Virtual rendering of rows and columns, pinned columns and column groups all depend on the DOM structure. Decide it with data before building features.
scope: Two small prototypes with 500 columns x 100,000 rows: a native <table> with spacer rows and columns, and a <div> grid with ARIA roles
Measure initial render time, scrolling frame rate, memory, and search and filter time over the shown text
Check that pinned columns and a two-level column header work in each prototype
Write the result and the decision in docs/
acceptance: A written decision with the measured numbers for both prototypes
A known plan for search speed and memory at full scale (for example a search index, debounce or a Web Worker)
tasks: Write a data generator for 500 columns x 100,000 rows
Build the <table> prototype with row and column virtualization
Build the <div> grid prototype with row and column virtualization
Add one pinned column and a two-level header to both
Measure render, scroll, memory, search and filter in Chrome and Safari

epics.title: Test setup for browser and speed tests
epics.why: jsdom does no layout, so layout and speed acceptance items need a real browser. Without these tests, no such item can pass.
scope: Playwright browser tests that run against the demo app, in Chrome and Safari (WebKit)
A benchmark script that measures render, scroll, search and filter times for the scale goal
pnpm scripts for both, so the pr skill can run them
acceptance: One pnpm script runs the browser tests and fails when a test fails
One pnpm script runs the benchmark and fails when a speed goal is missed
tasks: Add Playwright and a pnpm script for browser tests
Write a first browser test for the sticky header
Add a benchmark script with the scale goals as limits

epics.title: Virtual rendering and basic accessibility
epics.why: Only the rows and columns on screen are rendered, so the table stays fast at full scale.
scope: Row and column virtualization, based on the E02 decision
Keep the sticky header, overlay scroll bar space and fixed widths
ARIA grid roles with total row and column counts and each cell's index, so screen readers know the full size
acceptance: The demo shows 500 columns x 100,000 rows and meets the scale goals
A screen reader announces the correct row and column numbers

epics.title: Data pipeline and state model
epics.why: Search, filters, sort and pagination must work together in a fixed order, and consumers must be able to control their state.
scope: Pipeline steps: search, filter, sort, paginate
One pattern for controlled and uncontrolled state, used by every feature
Design the steps so a server mode can replace them later
acceptance: Unit tests show the steps run in the correct order
A feature can be used controlled and uncontrolled with the same API pattern

epics.title: Column types and custom cell render
epics.why: Dates, numbers and badges need formatting, and filters, sort and export need to know each column's type.
scope: Column type: text, number, date or category
Default formatting by type
Custom render function or formatter per column
One function that gives the shown text of a cell, used by search, filter and CSV export
acceptance: A column with a custom render shows it, and search finds its shown text

epics.title: Theming with CSS variables
epics.why: Apps must be able to match the table to their own design.
scope: Move all colors, borders, spacing and fonts into --wide-table-* variables with defaults
acceptance: An app changes the look by setting variables only, without overriding classes

epics.title: UI text overrides
epics.why: The built-in UI has its own text, such as "No columns" and filter labels. A public library must let apps change it, for example for other languages.
scope: A prop with all UI texts, with English defaults
acceptance: Every text in the built-in UI can be changed through the prop

epics.title: Sorting
epics.why: Users need to order rows by a column.
scope: Click a header to sort ascending, descending, or not sorted
Shift+click to sort by several columns
Sort by column type, with an optional custom compare function
acceptance: Sorting 100,000 rows takes under 200ms

epics.title: Pinned columns
epics.why: In a wide table, key columns such as ID or name must stay visible while the user scrolls right.
scope: Pin columns to the left or right in config
outOfScope: Pin and unpin from the UI
acceptance: Pinned columns stay in place during horizontal scrolling, also with the sticky header

epics.title: Column groups
epics.why: Hundreds of columns are easier to read and use in named groups.
scope: Groups in the column config, with several levels
Expand and collapse a group from its header
A column marked as a summary for its group stays visible when the group is collapsed
A collapsed group with no summary column shows as one narrow column with its name
acceptance: A three-level group header renders correctly with virtual columns
Collapsing a group shows only its summary columns, or the narrow column if it has none

epics.title: Hide and show columns
epics.why: With hundreds of columns, users must choose which ones they see.
scope: Columns tool panel: a side panel with all columns as a tree with their groups, show and hide checkboxes, and a search box
Hidden columns as state (controlled or uncontrolled)
outOfScope: Saving the state in the browser (apps can do it with the controlled mode)
acceptance: A user can find and hide one column out of 500 in a few seconds

epics.title: Free text search
epics.why: Users need to find rows without knowing which column has the value.
scope: One search box for the whole table
Search the shown text in visible columns only
Highlight the matching text
acceptance: Results show in under 200ms at full scale

epics.title: Column filters
epics.why: Users need to narrow rows by the values of one column.
scope: Value list filter for text and category columns: checkboxes for each unique value, with a search box
Condition filter for number and date columns: equals, greater than, less than, between
Filter state (controlled or uncontrolled) and a mark on filtered column headers
acceptance: Filters on several columns work together with search and sorting

epics.title: Row actions
epics.why: Apps need buttons per row, such as Edit, which opens the app's own modal.
scope: An actions column, pinned right, with buttons from config
onRowAction(action, row) callback
acceptance: The demo opens its own modal from an Edit button

epics.title: Documentation
epics.why: A public library needs docs to be used by others.
scope: API reference for every prop and column option
Examples for each feature
acceptance: Every public prop and column option is documented with an example

epics.title: Pagination
epics.why: Some apps want pages instead of one long scrolling list.
scope: An optional mode with page size and page controls
The page is state (controlled or uncontrolled)
acceptance: Changing search or filters goes back to page 1

epics.title: Status bar
epics.why: Users need to see how many rows match.
scope: A footer with total rows and rows after search and filters
outOfScope: Selected rows and sums of selected cells (needs E21)
acceptance: The counts update after search and filter changes

acceptance: Exporting 100,000 rows does not freeze the page

epics.title: Resize columns
epics.why: Users want to change column widths by dragging.
scope: Drag the header edge
Widths as state

epics.title: Reorder columns
epics.why: Users want to change the column order by dragging.
scope: Drag headers to reorder
A column stays inside its group

epics.title: Row selection
epics.why: Users want to select rows and act on them.
scope: Checkbox column
Select all rows after search and filters
Selected rows as state
Selected count in the status bar

epics.why: Users who do not use a mouse must be able to move between cells.
scope: Arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down between cells, with focus kept during virtual scrolling

epics.title: Row grouping
epics.why: Group rows by the value of one column.
scope: One level
Group rows with value and row count
Expand and collapse groups

epics.title: Multi-level row grouping with totals
epics.why: Group by several columns and show totals such as sum and average in group rows.

epics.title: Master/detail
epics.why: A row expands to show a detail panel below it.

epics.title: Server-side data mode
epics.why: Support data sets too large for the browser.
scope: The consumer gives a function that returns rows for the current search, filters, sort and page

epics.title: Built-in row edit modal
epics.why: Apps that do not want their own form could use a form generated from the column types.
